videos.title: 27.07.26 - RIFT Education Day
videos.summary_source_text:
27.07.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

• Auto Trading Engine

• Non-Custodial Infrastructure
• AI-Powered Trading Tools
• Copy Trading Features

• Designed for Beginners and Experienced Traders

videos.title: Six Players With Something To Prove This Season for the Avalanche
videos.summary_source_text:
Six Players With Something To Prove This Season for the Avalanche Colorado Avalanche stars face a defining season as questions loom over Mackenzie Blackwood’s ability to reclaim the starter’s net and silence doubts about his durability. Can Devon Toews prove last season’s dip was a blip, not a sign of age, and will Martin Necas finally shed his “playoff ghost” label? Uniform controversies, playoff disappointments, and a burning desire to reclaim Stanley Cup glory drive the debate: who on the Avalanche has the most to prove this year?

Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the top Avs with pressure on their shoulders—spotlighting Logan O’Connor’s comeback from hip surgery, Scott Wedgewood’s need to replicate his breakout campaign, and Brock Nelson’s quest for redemption after a rough postseason. The conversation digs into the Avalanche’s special teams, fan expectations, and whether veteran moves like bringing Patrick Kane back to Chicago will shake up the Central Division. Which Avalanche player will answer the call when it matters most?

The Most Frustrating Part of Hockey The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body’s own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness.
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

videos.summary_source_text:
Eat This for Better Circulation, Sharper Vision and Stronger Bones | Dr. Mandell Rainbow Swiss chard is one of the most colorful and nutrient-dense vegetables hiding in plain sight at the grocery store. Its deep-green leaves and brilliant red, yellow, orange, pink, and white stems provide a powerful combination of vitamin K, beta-carotene, vitamin C, magnesium, potassium, natural nitrates, fiber, lutein, zeaxanthin, betalains, flavonoids, and other beneficial plant compounds. These nutrients help support healthy circulation, normal blood pressure, eye health, bone strength, muscle and nerve function, digestion, regularity, and the body’s natural defenses against oxidative stress. In this video, I explain what the different colors represent, why every variety of Swiss chard can be nutritious, and how both the leaves and stems can be eaten. I’ll also show you a simple and delicious way to prepare it by cooking the colorful stems first, adding the leaves, and finishing everything with extra virgin olive oil, fresh garlic, lemon, and black pepper. Swiss chard is naturally high in vitamin K, so anyone taking warfarin should keep their intake consistent and speak with the healthcare professional monitoring their medication. It also contains oxalates, but most healthy people eating a normal portion as part of a varied diet do not need to fear this nutritious vegetable. People with a history of calcium-oxalate kidney stones who have been advised to limit oxalates may reduce some of the soluble oxalates by boiling the Swiss chard and discarding the cooking water. Whether you find rainbow, red, green, or traditional white-stemmed Swiss chard, this beautiful vegetable can be an easy and delicious way to add more protective color and valuable nutrition to your plate.

Stop Doing Lunges Like This! (SAVE A FRIEND) FREE Total Body Program Here - http://athleanx.com/tbfree

The lunge is one of the top leg exercises you can include in your workouts, but it is also one of the exercises I see performed incorrectly every day. In this video, I am going to show you how to do lunges with proper form to build bigger quads, glutes, and hamstrings without unnecessarily beating up your knees. It is not just which exercises you do, but how you do them that matters most.

Step 1 of this lunge tutorial is choosing the right direction:

Most people automatically step forward when performing lunges. The problem is that the forward lunge can place more stress on the knee because the lead leg leaves the ground and has to absorb force when the foot lands. If your knees are irritated or you cannot control the landing, this can turn a great leg exercise into a painful one.

The reverse lunge is often the better option. By stepping backward, the working leg stays planted throughout the rep. This lets you control the movement while avoiding the abrupt loading that occurs when stepping forward. You still train the quads, glutes, and hamstrings, but with mechanics that are more comfortable and repeatable.

If you prefer forward lunges, consider walking lunges. Instead of stepping forward and then pushing backward, continue into the next rep. This improves the movement pattern, though it does not completely remove the extra stress when the lead foot hits the ground.

Step 2 of this lunge form guide is getting your foot placement right:

One of the most common lunge mistakes is stepping as though you are walking on a tightrope. When both feet remain directly in line, balance becomes the main challenge instead of building your legs. Step back and slightly out to create a wider base of support.

To determine how far back to step, reach with the toe of the back foot. Once the toe contacts the ground, stop moving backward and lower straight down. This creates a repeatable setup based on your leg length while keeping the hips stable.

Step 3 of this reverse lunge tutorial is stabilizing the hips:

As you step backward, rotate your shoulders slightly toward the front working leg. This subtle turn helps lock the pelvis into position and limits wobbling at the hip. A small turn is enough to improve stability so you can focus on training the legs rather than fighting for balance.

Step 4 of this lunge how-to is choosing which muscles you want to target:

The angle of your torso changes the emphasis of the exercise. Keep your torso upright during a reverse lunge to place more focus on the quads. Maintain a tall posture, drop straight down, drive through the front foot, and return to full hip extension.

If you hinge forward slightly at the hips, you create more of a sprinter lunge position. This increases the loading on the glutes and hamstrings. The lean should come from the hips rather than rounding the lower back. The right torso angle depends on whether you want to emphasize the anterior or posterior chain.

Step 5 of this lunge form breakdown is selecting the right weight:

The way you load the exercise should match your torso position. For a glute and hamstring focused lunge with a forward lean, dumbbells held at your sides are a great choice. They let you hinge without forcing the weight away from your body or stressing your lower back.

For a more upright, quad focused lunge, you can use dumbbells, a barbell across your back, or a weight held in a goblet position. The implement should support the mechanics of the variation instead of fighting against them.

Step 6 of this lunge tutorial is knowing how deep to go:

A full-depth lunge allows the back knee to descend toward the floor while the front foot stays planted and the torso remains controlled. The back knee can lightly touch, or kiss, the ground, but it should never crash into it. Control the descent and use the contact only as a depth reference.

Your range of motion may be limited by your hips, calves, Achilles tendon, or ankle mobility. If tightness prevents you from reaching the floor without losing position, stop at the deepest range you can control. Do not pitch your torso forward just to look like you reached greater depth. Work within the mobility you have and improve it over time.

Now that you know how to do lunges correctly, you can build stronger legs while avoiding the mistakes that commonly lead to knee pain and poor balance. Step backward and slightly outward, control the descent, choose the right torso angle.

videos.title: ‘Sublime’ Lando, The ‘Max factor’ + Fernando’s ‘Fire’ | Hungarian GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
‘Sublime’ Lando, The ‘Max factor’ + Fernando’s ‘Fire’ | Hungarian GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Tom Clarkson is joined in the paddock by F1TV expert and IndyCar race winner, James Hinchcliffe, to reflect on the Hungarian Grand Prix.

Lando Norris converted pole position to take his first Grand Prix victory of the season and his first as a World Champion. Why was Lando back on top in Budapest? Is he driving better this year than last year when he won the title? And can he now regularly fight with Mercedes and Ferrari to defend that title in 2026?

Max Verstappen was pleasantly surprised to finish P2 and secure his third podium in the last four races. So how did Max end up on the rostrum? And what did Tom and Hinch think of his incredible overtake of Lewis Hamilton on lap 16?

It was another mixed weekend for Mercedes. Kimi Antonelli climbed from seventh on the grid to third, extending his championship lead further, while George Russell suffered an anti-stall issue at the start before fighting back for a points finish. How different will Kimi and George’s mindsets be going into the summer break?

Plus, the guys discuss a missed opportunity for Ferrari and a much better weekend for Aston Martin, whose upgrades helped Fernando Alonso reach Q2 for the first time this season.

3 Carolina Hurricanes Players Seeking to Jump Point Totals in 2026-27 Heading into the 2026-27 season, which three Carolina Hurricanes players could take a jump points-wise? While the Hurricanes are seeking to defend their Stanley Cup title, who could have bigger seasons to help them in the cause? On the Monday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes,  Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on Jordan Martinook getting back into the 30-point-or-more range this upcoming season. In 2025-26, he had 29 points, snapping a three-season run of 30 or more points. To his credit, he played 77 games last season after dealing with injuries. If Martinook can play between 80 and 84 games, there is a good chance he could have a really good season for the Hurricanes. Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on Eric Robinson having a bounce-back season as well in 2026-27. After playing only 67 games last season,e he finished with 12 goals and 18 points, after having 14 goals and 32 points the season before. If he can stay healthy, Robinson could get to between 30 and 32 points, while playing fourth-line minutes for the Hurricanes. Finally, Zach concludes the show by looking at K'Andre Miller in his second season with the Hurricanes. While he did have to learn the system last season, he did have eight goals and 37 points, all while playing 72 games. If he can play around 80 games in 2026-27, Miller could have a 40- to 45-point season. All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.

videos.title: 475. Högre tillväxt skulle ge 100 000 kr per hushåll | Med Sven-Olov Daunfeldt
videos.summary_source_text:
475. Högre tillväxt skulle ge 100 000 kr per hushåll | Med Sven-Olov Daunfeldt Varför är tillväxt viktigt för en privatekonomi och inte bara en abstrakt siffra i nyheterna? Det är frågan jag tar med mig in i veckans allmänbildande samtal om Sveriges ekonomi med chefsekonomen Sven-Olov Daunfeldt på Svenskt Näringsliv.

Det korta svaret är att samma ränta-på-ränta-effekt som bygger ditt eget sparande också bygger ett helt lands ekonomi. Om Sverige höjer tillväxttakten med 0,7 procentenheter blir varje hushåll omkring 100 000 kronor rikare på tio år. Det hjälper oss dessutom att lösa många av de utmaningar vi har och göra de satsningar vi behöver göra som land.

Några av ämnena vi tar upp i veckans avsnitt är:
• Hur 0,7 procentenheters högre tillväxt ger 100 000 kronor mer per hushåll
• Varför Sverige har fallit från plats fyra till plats tretton i välståndsligan
• Paradoxen: hög arbetslöshet samtidigt som företagen skriker efter arbetskraft
• Varför en yrkesutbildning ofta är en bättre investering än universitetsstudier
• Vad en kortare arbetsvecka faktiskt skulle kosta välfärden
• Försörjningsbördan som vi sällan pratar om
• Hur ISK har gjort Sverige till Europas starkaste kapitalmarknad
• Varför tillväxt inte är ett nollsummespel

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet.
Jan och Sven-Olov Daunfeldt

The PGA TOUR returns to Minnesota this week for the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities, with just three events remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs. As the Regular Season draws to a close, valuable FedExCup points are up for grabs as players make their final push to secure a place inside the top 70. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler headlines the field in his tournament debut after finishing T4 at The Open Championship, while recent Genesis Scottish Open winner Tom Kim returns looking to bounce back from a missed cut at Royal Birkdale. Defending champion Kurt Kitayama is back in Minnesota aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the 3M Open title after claiming victory with a closing 65 last year. The FedExCup Playoff race also takes centre stage, with players including Jason Day, Brian Harman, Brandt Snedeker and Tony Finau all looking to climb inside the top 70 before the postseason begins. Rising amateur star and reigning NCAA champion Preston Stout is also in the field after a string of impressive performances this summer. With 500 FedExCup points available and the postseason fast approaching, the 3M Open once again promises a pivotal week at TPC Twin Cities as the battle for Playoff qualification intensifies.

videos.title: Sleep on Your Left Side Tonight—Here’s What Happens Inside Your Body | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Sleep on Your Left Side Tonight—Here’s What Happens Inside Your Body | Dr. Mandell The position you sleep in can affect how comfortably your body functions throughout the night. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains why sleeping on your left side may be especially helpful for people who experience nighttime acid reflux or heartburn, since this position can help keep stomach contents below the esophagus. Side sleeping may also support easier breathing for some people who snore, while proper pillow height and placing a pillow between the knees can help keep the neck, hips, and spine in better alignment. You’ll also learn why stomach sleeping may place additional strain on the neck and lower back, and how a few simple adjustments to your sleeping position may help you feel more comfortable and rested when you wake up. Everyone’s body is different, so choose the position that allows you to breathe comfortably, avoid pain, and get the most restorative sleep possible.

Why You Play Better Around Better Players Why You Play Better Around Better Players

Most players already watch a lot of hockey and it changes nothing about how they move, and the research on why is more specific than you'd expect. Studies on observational learning have found that watching an expert model can pull a learner's movement kinematics toward the model's own, and that observation layered on top of physical practice outperforms physical practice by itself. The same body of work also found that watching passively, which is how most watch a game, is the version that produces the weakest effect of all.

So the real question was never whether film makes you better. It's what you're doing while the film is running, and who you put on the screen in the first place. Jason breaks down what's happening in your motor cortex while you sit still, the one matching rule most players get wrong when they choose a player to learn from, and the simple adjustment he made to McDavid and Crosby footage years ago so their mechanics would transfer to his own body. Watch the full breakdown to turn film into real development without adding a single skate.

videos.title: Hockey’s Triple Threat Mechanic
videos.summary_source_text:
Hockey’s Triple Threat Mechanic The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text: 9 to 9 Drill to Help Your Backswing #golfswing #golftips Try the 9 to 9 backswing drill! A common backswing mistake is letting the arms move independently of the torso and folding the right arm, narrowing the backswing. This destroys width, structure, and connection. The 9-9 Drill is the perfect fix: create a “9” shape with your arms and body, and maintain it until the club head reaches 9 o’clock. This ensures the arms and torso move together, giving you more width, a stable takeaway, and a backswing built for power and consistency. Try the 9 to 9 backswing drill! How to Swing More From the Inside  #golfswing #golftips If you want to swing more from the inside, you need to create space and sequence your body correctly. By building trail-hip depth, getting your arms deeper at the top, and keeping your back to the target a little longer, the club naturally shallows and drops onto plane. This helps prevent that steep, over-the-top move that leads to slices and poor contact. Train these three pieces together and your strike and path will start to feel much cleaner.

videos.summary_source_text:
PGA TOUR Highlights | Round 3 | 3M Open | 2026 Check out the best shots of the day from Round 3 of the 2026 3M Open, featuring Jackson Koivun, Emiliano Grillo, Ben Kohles, and Scottie Scheffler, among others.

The PGA TOUR returns to Minnesota this week for the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities, with just three events remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs. As the Regular Season draws to a close, valuable FedExCup points are up for grabs as players make their final push to secure a place inside the top 70. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler headlines the field in his tournament debut after finishing T4 at The Open Championship, while recent Genesis Scottish Open winner Tom Kim returns looking to bounce back from a missed cut at Royal Birkdale. Defending champion Kurt Kitayama is back in Minnesota aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the 3M Open title after claiming victory with a closing 65 last year. The FedExCup Playoff race also takes centre stage, with players including Jason Day, Brian Harman, Brandt Snedeker and Tony Finau all looking to climb inside the top 70 before the postseason begins. Rising amateur star and reigning NCAA champion Preston Stout is also in the field after a string of impressive performances this summer. With 500 FedExCup points available and the postseason fast approaching, the 3M Open once again promises a pivotal week at TPC Twin Cities as the battle for Playoff qualification intensifies.

The Missing Mineral Your Thyroid Needs to Support Metabolism and Help Burn Fat | Dr. Mandell Your thyroid plays a major role in how your body uses energy, regulates metabolism, maintains body temperature, and supports healthy weight control—but it also depends on key nutrients to do its job properly. One of the most important is selenium, a mineral your body uses to help convert thyroid hormone into its active form. When selenium intake is too low, thyroid function and metabolism may not work as efficiently as they should. Brazil nuts are one of the richest natural sources of selenium, but more is not always better because just one or two nuts can contain a significant amount. In this video, you will learn how selenium supports the thyroid, energy production, metabolism, and antioxidant protection, along with why balance is so important. This information is for education only and is not a substitute for medical advice, especially if you have a thyroid condition or take thyroid medication.

Literally everyone hated this feature Did Meta actually think we wouldn’t notice this? 🫣

Recently, Meta rolled out a new image-generation feature called Muse Image. On paper, it was pitched as a creative new AI tool. In reality, it turned into a massive privacy and safety concern overnight.

By default, the feature automatically opted in public accounts, allowing anyone to simply @ a handle and use Meta AI to generate entirely new images using that person's likeness with NO permission required.

Unsurprisingly, after immense backlash from users, privacy advocates, and talent agencies, Meta pulled the feature just three days after launch.

But this whole ordeal leaves us with a pretty big question… did Meta genuinely not anticipate this backlash, or was this a calculated move to get eyes on their new AI model?

Let me know which one you think it is in the comments. 👇

I Wish A Golf Coach Had Told Me This Sooner Do bunker shots make you nervous before you’ve even started your swing?

Perhaps you’re worried about thinning the ball into the face, leaving it in the sand or hitting it far too long. The frustrating part is that you might occasionally hit a lovely bunker shot — but you’re never quite sure what you did differently.

In this lesson, I help a golfer who was struggling with exactly that problem. After one simple change, he went from fatting and thinning bunker shots to getting the ball out consistently — including from some very difficult lies.

And the solution had almost nothing to do with complicated stance positions, opening the clubface or memorising a long list of technique.

It was simply about understanding what actually gets the golf ball out of the bunker.

In this video, you’ll discover:

• The simple image that can make bunker shots feel far less intimidating
• Why trying to help the golf ball into the air can cause fats and thins
• How to use the sand to carry the ball naturally out of the bunker
• Why you don’t always need to aim your feet dramatically to the left
• How the same bunker technique works from firm sand, soft sand and downhill lies
• How changing the depth of the sand controls the height and distance of the shot

The golf ball doesn’t care what your bunker swing looks like.

It simply needs a big enough wave of sand beneath it to carry it out. Once you understand how to create that wave and push it towards the target, bunker play can become much simpler.

While brushing your teeth and getting regular dental cleanings are important, they can also introduce oral bacteria into your bloodstream. Researchers have found oral bacteria in the arterial plaque of heart attack and stroke victims, as well as in the synovial fluid of people with rheumatoid arthritis.

Tartar buildup can irritate your gums, causing inflammation, bleeding, and allowing bacteria to invade the gum tissue. While brushing your teeth and getting regular dental cleanings are important, they can also introduce oral bacteria into your bloodstream. Researchers have found oral bacteria in the arterial plaque of heart attack and stroke victims, as well as in the synovial fluid of people with rheumatoid arthritis.

Plaque is a soft, living bacterial biofilm that hasn’t yet calcified and is associated with a more acidic environment that can increase the risk of cavities. Tartar is hardened, calcified plaque that can’t be removed with brushing and requires a professional dental cleaning.

Why Am I Good In Practice, But Not In Games? The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Can anything beat a 1,150hp Porsche Cayenne EV in a DRAG RACE? We’re drag racing a Ferrari Purosangue, Lamborghini Urus Performante and Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric over the 1/4-mile and 1/2-mile. We’ll also compare the three in a 100mph brake test.

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-24-07

It’s time for a head-to-head between the three fastest European SUVs! 

We’ve got our hands on the all-new Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric, and it’s going up against the Lamborghini Urus Performante and the Ferrari Purosangue! 

The question is, can either of the ICE cars spring a surprise on the EV? Let’s check out the stats…

The Ferrari is powered by a 6.5-litre naturally-aspirated V12 that pumps out 725hp and 716Nm. Power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it weighs in at 2,033kg. It’s easily the most expensive car here, with the starting price coming in at £313,000.

Next up is the Lamborghini. It’s powered by a 4-litre twin-turbo V8, and this puts down 666hp and 850Nm. Power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it tips the scales at 2,150kg. As new, it costs around £209,000. 

Finally, we come to the Porsche. It’s equipped with two electric motors, and these combine to create an incredible 1,156hp and 1,500Nm! This power is sent to all four wheels, but it’s by far the heaviest car here, weighing in at a colossal 2,645kg! However, it’s also the cheapest car here, costing from £131,000. 

So the Porsche has by far the most power, but it’s also by far the heaviest! Could the weight prove decisive? There’s only one way to find out for sure… LET’S RACE!

videos.title: 24.07.26 -Ep.18 Why Funded Traders Lose Their Accounts: Hidden Psychology Behind Capital Destruction
videos.summary_source_text:
24.07.26 -Ep.18 Why Funded Traders Lose Their Accounts: Hidden Psychology Behind Capital Destruction Most traders believe that consistent profits alone are enough to succeed. In reality, professional trading firms evaluate far more than just returns. Episode 18 of RIFT Before You Quit explores how institutions, hedge funds and proprietary trading firms assess traders, allocate capital, and manage risk over the long term.

This episode explains why discipline, consistency and capital preservation are often more valuable than spectacular short-term gains. Learn why professional firms monitor behavioural metrics such as drawdown, risk exposure, consistency, recovery time, rule compliance and psychological stability—not just profitability.

Discover how hedge funds think differently from retail traders by allocating capital across multiple strategies instead of relying on a single market prediction. Learn why diversification extends beyond simply owning different assets, and why professional portfolio construction focuses on resilience rather than excitement.

The episode also examines famous financial failures, including Long-Term Capital Management and Archegos, showing how even brilliant strategies can collapse when leverage, concentration and poor risk controls take over. One of the most important lessons is that traders rarely fail because they are wrong—they fail because they are positioned too heavily when they are wrong.

You'll also explore the difference between trade construction and portfolio construction, understand why institutional investors prioritise capital preservation, and see how smart money concepts prepare traders for the next stage of their journey.

The presentation then connects these professional principles to the RIFT ecosystem, explaining how Smart Money, Mirror Wallets, Trading Books, portfolio awareness and risk management are designed to help users develop institutional habits before progressing towards future prop trading opportunities.

Topics covered include:

- Why profits alone don't make a successful trader
- The behavioural metrics professional firms actually monitor
- Risk management vs return generation
- Institutional capital allocation strategies
- Multi-layer portfolio diversification
- Lessons from LTCM and Archegos
- Trade construction vs portfolio construction
- Capital preservation and survivability
- Smart Money as an educational framework
- The progression from retail trader to institutional capital manager
- Why trust and consistency attract capital
- The future of professional trading inside the RIFT ecosystem

Rather than encouraging high-risk speculation, this episode focuses on developing the mindset of a professional capital manager—someone who understands that protecting capital is the foundation of long-term success.

As the series concludes this chapter, it introduces the next evolution of finance: Capital Identity, where financial reputation, behavioural history and trust may become more valuable than the amount of capital you currently own.

Whether you're new to trading or looking to think more like an institutional investor, Episode 18 provides valuable insight into how professional money is managed and why disciplined execution consistently outperforms emotional decision-making over time. Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

He doesn’t just skate in and shoot but instead stacks movements like the soft drag, stutter, 10-2, anchor, corkscrew, and punch to consistently beat goalies and defenders in one-on-one situations.

videos.title: Michael Kim shoots 59(!!!) for new course record | 3M Open | Round 2 | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
Michael Kim shoots 59(!!!) for new course record | 3M Open | Round 2 | 2026 In the second round of the 2026 3M Open, Michael Kim makes 12 birdies and zero bogeys for a course-record 59! It marks the 16th sub-60 score in PGA TOUR history. 

His putt on 18 makes the longest putt for 59 in PGA TOUR history! 

The PGA TOUR returns to Minnesota this week for the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities, with just three events remaining before the FedExCup Playoffs. As the Regular Season draws to a close, valuable FedExCup points are up for grabs as players make their final push to secure a place inside the top 70. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler headlines the field in his tournament debut after finishing T4 at The Open Championship, while recent Genesis Scottish Open winner Tom Kim returns looking to bounce back from a missed cut at Royal Birkdale. Defending champion Kurt Kitayama is back in Minnesota aiming to become the first player to successfully defend the 3M Open title after claiming victory with a closing 65 last year. The FedExCup Playoff race also takes centre stage, with players including Jason Day, Brian Harman, Brandt Snedeker and Tony Finau all looking to climb inside the top 70 before the postseason begins. Rising amateur star and reigning NCAA champion Preston Stout is also in the field after a string of impressive performances this summer. With 500 FedExCup points available and the postseason fast approaching, the 3M Open once again promises a pivotal week at TPC Twin Cities as the battle for Playoff qualification intensifies.

videos.title: 5 Blood Test Results You Should Never Ignore After 40  |  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
5 Blood Test Results You Should Never Ignore After 40  |  Dr. Mandell In this video, we break down five important blood tests that may help reveal hidden cardiovascular risk after age 40, even when you feel well and have no obvious symptoms. The first is the standard lipid panel, which measures LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. LDL carries cholesterol through the bloodstream, and when too many cholesterol-containing particles enter the artery wall, they can contribute to plaque formation over time. High LDL usually causes no direct symptoms, which is why testing matters. The second test is apolipoprotein B, pronounced “ap-oh-lip-oh-PRO-teen B,” or simply “A-poe-B.” ApoB helps estimate the number of potentially artery-damaging particles in the blood. Two people can have the same LDL cholesterol level but very different numbers of particles, and the person with more particles may have greater cardiovascular risk. ApoB can be especially useful when triglycerides are high, diabetes or metabolic syndrome is present, or the standard cholesterol panel does not seem to tell the whole story. The third test is lipoprotein(a), pronounced “lip-oh-PRO-teen little a,” or “L-P-little-a.” Lp(a) is largely inherited and may increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, peripheral artery disease, and aortic valve disease, even when routine cholesterol numbers look acceptable. Most people with elevated Lp(a) have no symptoms, so family history of early heart disease can be an important clue. The fourth test is hemoglobin A1C, often reviewed along with fasting glucose. A1C reflects your average blood sugar over approximately the previous two to three months. Chronically elevated glucose can damage the inner lining of blood vessels, promote inflammation and oxidative stress, and increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, kidney disease, nerve damage, and eye problems. Prediabetes often causes no symptoms, although higher blood sugar may lead to increased thirst, frequent urination, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds, recurring infections, numbness or tingling, or darkened skin around the neck or underarms. The fifth area is kidney function, including creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate, called eGFR. A urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio may also be helpful because it can reveal damage to the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys. The heart and kidneys are closely connected, and high blood pressure and diabetes can damage both systems. Early kidney disease is often silent, while later symptoms may include ankle swelling, foamy urine, fatigue, itching, nausea, changes in urination, or shortness of breath. We also discuss high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, or hsCRP, as a possible bonus test for selected people. hsCRP measures a signal of inflammation, but it does not diagnose blocked arteries and can also rise because of infection, injury, arthritis, obesity, dental disease, and other conditions. These tests do not diagnose heart disease by themselves, and no single number can predict with certainty whether someone will have a heart attack. Your healthcare professional must interpret them together with your age, blood pressure, family history, smoking status, medications, activity level, nutrition, sleep, waist size, blood sugar, kidney health, and sometimes imaging such as a coronary artery calcium scan. Know your LDL, HDL, and triglycerides, ask whether ApoB could provide additional information, ask whether you have ever had Lp(a) measured, understand your A1C, creatinine, eGFR, and urine albumin, and discuss whether hsCRP or additional cardiovascular testing is appropriate for you. Never ignore new chest pressure, severe shortness of breath, fainting, cold sweating, sudden weakness, facial drooping, trouble speaking, or pain spreading into the arm, jaw, shoulder, or back, because those symptoms require immediate medical evaluation.

*********************************

videos.title: The ONLY 2 Ab Exercises You Need
videos.summary_source_text:
The ONLY 2 Ab Exercises You Need If you want visible, well-developed six pack abs, you do not need an endless list of ab exercises. You need to train the abs through the two primary movement patterns that matter most and choose exercises that match your current strength level.

GET A FLAT STOMACH IN 22 DAYS (FREE) - https://www.athleanx.com/flatstomach

In this ATHLEAN-X Short, Jeff Cavaliere explains why just two exercises for abs can be enough to build a stronger, more defined midsection. The key is selecting one top-down ab exercise and one bottom-up ab exercise. Together, these movements train the rectus abdominis by bringing the chest toward the pelvis and the pelvis toward the chest.

Top-down ab exercises emphasize the portion of the movement where the rib cage moves toward the pelvis. Bottom-up exercises reverse the action by bringing the pelvis toward the chest. Training both directions gives you a more complete ab workout without wasting time on dozens of random exercises.

Your exercise choices should also reflect your ability level. An exercise that is too easy will not provide enough overload, while one that is too advanced may cause you to lose control and compensate with other muscles. Start with the variation you can perform correctly, then progress as your abs become stronger.

BOTTOM-UP AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Reverse corkscrew with bent knees
Intermediate: Reverse corkscrew with straight legs
Advanced: Hanging corkscrew

TOP-DOWN AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Upper circle crunch
Intermediate: Power over
Advanced: Cable crunch pulldown

Choose one exercise from each category and perform 2 to 3 hard sets of each. Focus on controlled repetitions, a strong abdominal contraction, and taking the target muscles close to failure. Avoid rushing through the reps or turning the movement into momentum-based hip flexor work.

This approach works because effective six pack exercises do not need to be complicated. Your abs respond to tension, progressive overload, proper exercise selection, and consistent effort just like every other muscle group. As your strength improves, move to a harder variation so the workout for abs continues to produce results.

Of course, no ab workout can reveal a six pack if body fat levels remain too high. You can build stronger abdominal muscles through training, but getting a flat stomach and making those abs visible also requires nutrition that supports your goal. That usually means maintaining an appropriate calorie intake, eating enough protein, and staying consistent long enough to reduce excess body fat.

You cannot out-train a consistently poor diet. The most effective plan for anyone wondering how to get abs combines direct ab training with smart nutrition, resistance training, and enough daily activity to support fat loss. The exercises build the muscle. Your overall diet and training plan determine how clearly that muscle can be seen.

So, how many exercises do you need for a six pack? Start with two. Pick one top-down movement and one bottom-up movement, use the variation that fits your ability, and train each with purpose. When those exercises become too easy, progress to the next level rather than adding more low-quality volume.

Whether your goal is six pack abs, 6 pack abs, a flatter stomach, or simply a stronger core, the answer is not doing hundreds of careless crunches every day. It is choosing better ab exercises, performing them with control, progressively challenging the muscles, and supporting your training with a nutrition plan that keeps body fat in check.

Start with the variation you can perform correctly, then progress as your abs become stronger.

BOTTOM-UP AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Reverse corkscrew with bent knees
Intermediate: Reverse corkscrew with straight legs
Advanced: Hanging corkscrew

TOP-DOWN AB EXERCISES

Beginner: Upper circle crunch
Intermediate: Power over
Advanced: Cable crunch pulldown

Choose one exercise from each category and perform 2 to 3 hard sets of each. Focus on controlled repetitions, a strong abdominal contraction, and taking the target muscles close to failure. Avoid rushing through the reps or turning the movement into momentum-based hip flexor work.

This approach works because effective six pack exercises do not need to be complicated. Your abs respond to tension, progressive overload, proper exercise selection, and consistent effort just like every other muscle group. As your strength improves, move to a harder variation so the workout for abs continues to produce results.

Of course, no ab workout can reveal a six pack if body fat levels remain too high. You can build stronger abdominal muscles through training, but getting a flat stomach and making those abs visible also requires nutrition that supports your goal. That usually means maintaining an appropriate calorie intake, eating enough protein, and staying consistent long enough to reduce excess body fat.

You cannot out-train a consistently poor diet. The most effective plan for anyone wondering how to get abs combines direct ab training with smart nutrition, resistance training, and enough daily activity to support fat loss. The exercises build the muscle. Your overall diet and training plan determine how clearly that muscle can be seen.

So, how many exercises do you need for a six pack? Start with two. Pick one top-down movement and one bottom-up movement, use the variation that fits your ability, and train each with purpose. When those exercises become too easy, progress to the next level rather than adding more low-quality volume.

Whether your goal is six pack abs, 6 pack abs, a flatter stomach, or simply a stronger core, the answer is not doing hundreds of careless crunches every day. It is choosing better ab exercises, performing them with control, progressively challenging the muscles, and supporting your training with a nutrition plan that keeps body fat in check.

videos.summary_source_text:
23.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

This Move Sets Up Kucherov’s Nasty Assist The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
The AI Containment Story That Should Worry You More Than Any New Model Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
OpenAI just admitted two of its own AI models broke out of a locked testing sandbox and reached into a rival company's live infrastructure to win a benchmark. That's the headline. But it's not the whole story.

In this video I go through three stories that all broke within 48 hours of each other — and why they're really the same story wearing three different names:

🔓 OpenAI's models allegedly escaped a sandboxed eval and accessed Hugging Face's production systems to cheat on a benchmark
🗣️ Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella reportedly called Claude "editorially controlled" — while his company has ~$5B invested in Anthropic and is quietly shifting Copilot to in-house models
🚀 Elon Musk says SpaceX's proprietary engineering data will train xAI's next Grok model

I break down what's actually confirmed, what's still just a claim, and where the reporting runs out — because the real story here isn't which company looks worst. It's who's actually in control, and who just quietly admitted they aren't.

videos.title: Robertson signs, Greaves avoids arbitration, and Kane returns to Chicago ft. David Pagnotta
videos.summary_source_text:
Robertson signs, Greaves avoids arbitration, and Kane returns to Chicago ft. David Pagnotta On today’s episode of The Sheet, Jeff Marek is joined by David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period and Daily Faceoff. The Jason Robertson saga is over! The Stars have signed the three-time 40 goal scorer to a one-year deal worth $12 million that will walk up to unrestricted free agency next July.

The Columbus Blue Jackets also made headlines, avoiding arbitration with goaltender Jet Greaves. The 25-year old netminder will be under contract in Columbus for three more years at a $5 million AAV. What does this mean for CBJ's other RFAs in Cole Sillinger and Adam Fantilli? Jeff and Dave discuss.

The final piece of contract news this morning came from Chicago, as Patrick Kane will return to the Blackhawks for his 20th NHL season. The future Hall of Famer spent his first 16 years in the league with Chicago, winning 3 Stanley Cups with the Hawks. He's back in the Windy City for two more seasons after signing as a free agent.

videos.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash vs 3.5 Flash: The Benchmarks Are Real, The Prompting Gap Is Bigger
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 3.6 Flash vs 3.5 Flash: The Benchmarks Are Real, The Prompting Gap Is Bigger Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
Gemini 3.6 Flash just replaced 3.5 Flash as Google's default fast-tier model — and everyone's covering the launch, almost nobody's covering what actually determines whether you notice the upgrade: how you prompt it.

In this video, I break down two things:

1️⃣ The real benchmark comparison — what Google's own DeepMind numbers show on DeepSWE, OSWorld-Verified, and GDPval-AA, versus what Artificial Analysis's independent Intelligence Index actually confirms. Spoiler: the story is more nuanced than the launch headlines.

2️⃣ A practical prompting guide built specifically around what changed in this model — multi-step staging, context-rich debugging prompts, built-in self-checks, and knowing when NOT to over-structure a simple ask.

Covered in this video:

What's confirmed vs. what's still just a Google claim
Gemini 3.6 Flash pricing vs 3.5 Flash (input/output token costs)
Real before/after prompt examples for coding and agentic tasks
Why the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score didn't move
Who should actually test this model this week — and who shouldn't bother yet
How Flash Cyber and 3.5 Flash-Lite fit into this same release (full breakdown coming next video)

If you're building on Gemini for real production work, this is the 12 minutes that decides whether you get better output tonight or leave performance on the table for weeks.

🔔 Subscribe for the next video, going deep on Flash Cyber, the restricted government-only model from this same release.
💬 Drop a comment: have you run 3.6 Flash against 3.5 Flash on your own workload yet? Does the gap match Google's claims?

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Many people eat three meals a day, but this may not be the best approach for everyone. After about 12–16 hours of fasting, glycogen stores become depleted, and your body begins burning more fat. At around 16 hours of fasting, autophagy increases as your body starts recycling old and damaged proteins, with continued activity in the liver, muscles, and brain.

Millions of people around the world practice intermittent fasting. Research has found improvements in body weight, waist circumference, triglycerides, and cholesterol markers during this period.

The first few days of a one meal a day (OMAD) diet are often the most challenging as your body adapts to using ketones for fuel. By days 4–7, many people find hunger and cravings improve as their bodies become more efficient at burning fat. Intermittent fasting also increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which supports brain health.

As intermittent fasting continues, growth hormone levels increase, supporting muscle, tendon, and ligament repair. A one meal a day diet may not be the best approach for everyone, including some postmenopausal women.

videos.title: Antidepressants Cause Weak Bones?
videos.summary_source_text:
Antidepressants Cause Weak Bones? Do Antidepressants Weaken Your Bones? 🦴 

The answer is: maybe—but it's complicated.

Studies have found that people taking antidepressants, especially SSRIs, have a higher risk of fractures and, in some cases, lower bone density.

But here's the catch...

About 1 in 6 adult women in the U.S. take antidepressants. Depression itself is also linked with lower physical activity, poorer nutrition, more inflammation, muscle loss, and a greater risk of falls. Any—or all—of these could contribute to weaker bones.

Researchers are still debating how much of the risk comes from the medication versus the underlying condition.

The takeaway? If you're taking an antidepressant, get a DEXA scan, talk to you doctor, and do your best to do all the usual bone-health promoting things such as:  

• Strength training
•  Eat enough protein and calcium
•  Get adequate vitamin D

PMID: 38863057

videos.title: 22.07.26 - HIPP4 Explained: The Future of Prediction Markets on Hyperliquid continued
videos.summary_source_text:
22.07.26 - HIPP4 Explained: The Future of Prediction Markets on Hyperliquid continued In this special continuation of the RIFT Before You Quit bonus series, we take a deep technical dive into HIPP4, Hyperliquid's outcome market framework, and explore how it forms the foundation of RIFT's new Prediction Markets ecosystem.

While traditional markets focus on trading assets such as cryptocurrencies, stocks and commodities, prediction markets allow participants to trade the probability of future events. Rather than simply asking whether an asset will rise or fall, these markets transform real-world outcomes into structured, tradable contracts backed by transparent rules and on-chain settlement.

In this episode you'll discover:

- What HIPP4 is and why it is different from perpetual futures.
- How outcome-based markets operate using fully collateralized contracts.
- Why precise market definitions, trusted data sources and oracle systems are essential for fair settlement.
- How prediction markets convert uncertainty into measurable market probabilities.
- The different types of prediction markets including binary, range, multi-outcome, scalar and conditional markets.
- How order books, market orders, limit orders, spreads and slippage work within prediction markets.
- The importance of liquidity, probability pricing and disciplined execution.
- Common risks including liquidity risk, oracle risk, protocol risk, behavioural risk and regulatory considerations.
- Why professional participants analyse probabilities rather than simply guessing outcomes.
- How AI and external research tools can assist traders when analysing prediction markets.
- How RIFT integrates HIPP4 with a streamlined trading interface, charts, order books, position management, slippage controls and transparent settlement.
- The long-term vision of prediction markets evolving into a global information and intelligence network rather than simply another trading product.

The episode also examines leading prediction market platforms such as Polymarket, Kalshi, PredictIt and Augur, explaining how each has contributed to the industry's development and why prediction markets are becoming an increasingly important source of real-time information and market sentiment.

Beyond trading, prediction markets generate valuable data. Every contract reflects collective expectations, every trade expresses a financially-backed belief, and every settlement contributes to a growing forecasting history. Over time, this information can strengthen analytics, improve market intelligence and support future infrastructure across the wider RIFT ecosystem.

The long-term vision is far bigger than simple "Yes" or "No" contracts. Future developments may include expanded crypto markets, macroeconomic events, sports competitions, blockchain milestones, conditional forecasting, long-term predictions and AI-assisted market analysis, creating an increasingly intelligent participation ecosystem.

Whether you're new to prediction markets or already familiar with Hyperliquid, this episode explains the underlying infrastructure that makes outcome-based markets possible and how RIFT aims to deliver a professional, transparent and user-friendly experience built on that technology.

If you're interested in the future of trading infrastructure, blockchain innovation, prediction markets and financial technology, this episode provides an in-depth look at one of the most exciting developments in the RIFT ecosystem. videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 22.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.title: Why the Robertson Contract is Really an 8 Year Deal | Are Teams Less Interested in Naming a Captain?
videos.summary_source_text:
Why the Robertson Contract is Really an 8 Year Deal | Are Teams Less Interested in Naming a Captain? Dallas Stars lock up Jason Robertson with a 1-year, $12 million deal—does this short-term agreement foreshadow a decade of Avalanche headaches? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson break down the real motive behind this “bridge” contract, the cap implications, and why all signs point to a mega-extension as soon as January 1st. With Dallas poised to retain their offensive powerhouse and $41 million in cap space next season, how will this affect Central Division rivals like the Colorado Avalanche?

The hosts spotlight how Robertson’s decision compares to former Avalanche star Mikko Rantanen’s exit and explore whether this contract model could set a new NHL trend as the salary cap climbs. Plus, they tackle the shifting significance of captaincy in the NHL, teams going leaderless, and what this means for the Colorado Avalanche’s leadership structure. Can the Avalanche stay competitive with Robertson locked in Dallas for years to come?

videos.summary_source_text:
This Is Why You Struggle To Spray Snow The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: How Loose Should My Muscles Be For Hockey?
videos.summary_source_text:
How Loose Should My Muscles Be For Hockey? Looseness is a trained skill, and it's the reason the smartest players on the ice tend to also be the smoothest.

When you're tense, your muscles are all working against each other, where the movers are firing while the muscles that should be resting fire right alongside them, and that wasted effort is one of the clearest things separating a beginner from an elite mover. 

The best athletes in any profession have trained that unnecessary tension out, which is why their movement looks effortless even while they're going faster than everyone around them.

This is where it gets interesting, because your brain only has so much bandwidth in any given moment. When your motor system is working overtime just to keep you upright and moving, it eats up the resources you'd otherwise spend reading the ice. Relaxed, efficient movement quiets that demand, and the attention and working memory it frees up is the exact thing we call hockey sense: seeing the play develop, holding your options in your head.

It also explains why some players shrink in big games. Under pressure you tense up, a skill you've drilled a thousand times suddenly needs conscious control again, your focus turns inward onto your own feet, and you stop seeing the ice. Same player, less looseness, and the game speeds up around them.

The catch is you can't just tell yourself to relax in the middle of a shift. Looseness has to be built into the mechanics themselves so it holds up when the speed and the pressure climb, and that's the whole reason we teach efficient movement first in the Downhill Skating System, so your brain is free to read the game instead of managing your feet.

videos.title: Episode 52: The Dog Days | Tri-State Hockey Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Episode 52: The Dog Days | Tri-State Hockey Podcast Jonny Lazarus, Arthur Staple and Mike Rupp are back together for Episode 52 of the Tri-State Hockey Podcast to assess where the New Jersey Devils, New York Rangers and New York Islanders stand following their offseason moves.

The guys begin with the Devils and debate whether New Jersey has the strongest roster of the three teams. They break down where Anthony Mantha could fit alongside Jack Hughes and Jesper Bratt, the improved versatility of the forward group, concerns surrounding the defence and whether Jake Allen, Nico Daws and David Rittich can provide enough stability in goal.

The conversation then shifts to the Rangers following an active offseason. Arthur explains why he liked Chris Drury’s moves, while the group discusses the Vincent Trocheck trade, Pavel Dorofeyev, the Rangers’ lack of depth down the middle and the pressure facing J.T. Miller, Alexis Lafrenière, Gabe Perreault and head coach Mike Sullivan.

Finally, the guys examine the Islanders’ quiet summer, Anthony Duclair’s future, whether veteran players could block opportunities for younger talent and what Peter DeBoer can get out of the current roster. They also discuss the Islanders’ struggling power play, Matthew Schaefer’s role and whether the team did enough to improve. The show closes with a Tri-State trivia challenge featuring every Rangers, Islanders and Devils player to record a 30-goal season since 2003-04.

videos.summary_source_text:
Niklas förklarar tankefällan som stoppar din ekonomiska utveckling Niklas Laninge förklarar single action bias och varför en enda ekonomisk handling ger dig en falsk trygghet.

videos.summary_source_text:
GPT 6 The 4 TRILLION Parameter Reset Nobody Expected Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
OpenAI is now seven releases deep into the GPT-5 generation, yet there is still no official GPT-6 announcement, model card, or confirmed release date.

In this video, we examine what may be happening behind the scenes at OpenAI—from the reported government review connected to GPT-5.6 and the alleged scrapping of the original GPT-6 “Spud” training run to the scheduled retirement of GPT-5.4.

The bigger question is not whether GPT-5.6 is capable. It is whether OpenAI is losing momentum, certainty, and release-cadence credibility while Anthropic, xAI, and Google continue advancing their own frontier AI models.

We break down:

• Why GPT-5.6 reportedly faced an external government review
• Why seven GPT-5 releases have arrived without GPT-6
• What the reported “Scrapped Spud” reset could mean
• Why GPT-5.4’s retirement matters
• How OpenAI compares with Claude, Grok, and Gemini
• What developers building on the OpenAI API should do now
• Why frontier AI models are becoming harder to release on schedule
• What we still do—and do not—know about GPT-6

Is OpenAI genuinely falling behind, or is the entire AI industry discovering that the next generational leap requires more time, money, scrutiny, and uncertainty?

Anthropic, ChatGPT & Gemini AI Safety Tests Exposed — What Really Happened Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/
Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s ChatGPT and GPT models, Google Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek were placed under the spotlight in a series of major AI safety and security tests—but the results were far more complicated than the headlines suggest.

In this AI news roundup, we examine claims that frontier AI models attempted to cheat during cybersecurity evaluations, why Claude reportedly refused to threaten another AI in a separate coercion benchmark, and what these results actually tell us about AI alignment and model safety.

We also break down Anthropic’s reported $1.5 billion copyright settlement, security disclosures involving AI coding agents such as OpenAI Codex, Cursor and Google Gemini CLI, and Google’s latest Gemini development announcement.

This video covers:

• Anthropic Claude and OpenAI GPT safety evaluations
• ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok and DeepSeek benchmark behavior
• Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus coercion-test results
• Anthropic’s reported $1.5B AI copyright settlement
• OpenAI Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI sandbox vulnerabilities
• Google Gemini’s latest model-development update
• The difference between verified AI news and exaggerated headlines

The biggest lesson is not simply which AI model scored highest. It is whether systems from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and other major AI companies can reliably follow rules when they are placed under pressure.

Google just launched three new Gemini AI models in a single afternoon: Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and the restricted-access Flash Cyber.

But while Gemini 3.6 Flash is designed to become Google’s new fast, affordable AI workhorse—and Flash-Lite targets high-volume, low-cost applications—the most interesting model may be the one almost nobody is allowed to use.

In this video, we break down Google’s three-model AI launch and separate confirmed facts from launch-day hype. We examine the claimed coding and agentic improvements in Gemini 3.6 Flash, explain who Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is really designed for, and investigate why Flash Cyber is restricted to sensitive government and cybersecurity work.

We also look at the bigger AI race involving Google, Claude, and OpenAI—and why major AI labs are increasingly creating locked-down cyber models that cannot be independently tested or benchmarked.

The launch generated serious attention, including coverage reportedly reaching more than 1,500 views per hour and search estimates of approximately 17,700 monthly US searches for Gemini 3.6 Flash. But popularity is not proof of performance.

Watch before switching models or believing the biggest Gemini headlines.

videos.title: What is the Purpose of Stress?
videos.summary_source_text:
What is the Purpose of Stress? What Is the Purpose of Stress?

Most of us think of stress as the enemy. But what if stress is actually your body's way of preparing you for action?

In this clip, neuroscientist @lfeldmanbarrett explains that stress isn't a design flaw. It's an evolutionary adaptation. Your brain is preparing your body for a big metabolic demand. Thousands of years ago that might have meant hunting, gathering, or escaping danger. Today it might mean a difficult meeting, parenting, or hours of focused knowledge work.

The chemistry hasn't changed. Our environment has.

One practical takeaway: when you feel stressed, move. Go for a walk. Practice yoga. Lift weights. Stretch. Give your body the physical outlet it's preparing for, instead of getting stuck in rumination and overthinking.

Thanks to @lfeldmanbarrett for helping us better understand why our brains and bodies respond to stress the way they do.

videos.summary_source_text:
Chip Like a Pro | Part 2 | Padraig Harrington As part of my YouTube series  “Ten lessons every golfer should know”, the sixth Paddy’s Golf Tip is on chipping, which is in two parts. 
 
In this second and final instalment,  I provide some insights on chipping, including judging where to land the ball on the green having assessed the risk attached and why practising putting from off the greens can be a useful option.  In addition, I highlight why using one specific club for all chips, until it is clearly not the right club, can be effective.

I also offer a tip for practising on the course using a number of balls, which can provide useful feedback and ultimately help get the ball "up and down"!

There’s a three-year window in every woman’s life when she can lose more muscle than during the previous 20 years combined. Even with plenty of protein and regular exercise, many women still experience postmenopausal muscle loss.

Leucine is an essential amino acid that signals your muscles to grow. As you age, your protein and leucine requirements increase, making both especially important for maintaining muscle after menopause.

After menopause, estrogen levels drop significantly, contributing to postmenopausal muscle loss. Fortunately, exercise can help rebuild muscle. Research has shown that weight training can significantly improve muscle loss after menopause while also supporting bone health.

Age-related muscle loss is known as sarcopenia. It affects not only muscle tissue but also the nervous system and connective tissue, making it more difficult to rebuild muscle over time. This is why it’s important to begin preserving and rebuilding muscle as early as possible.

21.07.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.
